messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways, 35 mph on city streets.
• “No speed limit” zones exist in some rural areas. | Exceeding posted limits can lead to fines, points, and possible license suspension. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %). | Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules apply at intersections without signals. | Failure to yield can lead to fines and points. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are prohibited unless the vehicle has a fog‑light system. | Non‑compliance can result in a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid license and insurance. | Unregistered vehicles can be towed and fined. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in no‑parking zones.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• In Texas, stopping is required in both directions. | Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Points are added for violations (e.g., 1 point for speeding 5–10 mph over limit).
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | No‑fault insurance is not required, but proof of insurance is mandatory. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles require a valid motorcycle endorsement.
• Commercial vehicles have additional regulations (e.g., hours‑of‑service). | | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)**: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) – for road conditions and updates. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)**: [https://www.txdmv.gov](https://www.txdmv.gov) – for licensing, registration, and insurance requirements. - **Texas Transportation Code**: Available online for the full legal text. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
